question.text: For a WELL-DIVERSIFIED portfolio, Sharpe and Treynor ratios tend to:

explanation.text: The Logic: For a completely well-diversified portfolio, Sharpe and Treynor give identical rankings because total risk and systematic risk would be the same. The Trap: Ranking differences between Sharpe and Treynor are attributable to differing levels of diversification rather than to one of the ratios being "wrong". Note: The ratios measure different risk concepts (total vs. systematic), so identical rankings hold only in the fully-diversified case.
